summary: Repository baseline exposes complete catalog records, including hidden products and internal fields. Proposed protections are emulator-only and have not been deployed.

findings.issue: Anonymous reads of jewelry return every field, including mixed notes, cost, storage and media references; showInShop does not restrict access.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit public projection and administrator-only canonical records, with separately approved migration and rules.

findings.issue: Public view/favorite code attempts direct product writes, while repository rules require administrator access.
findings.recommendation: Plan a bounded server-side metrics endpoint; do not relax product-write rules. Production behavior is not write-tested.

findings.issue: The fallback admin-email authorization does not check email_verified.
findings.recommendation: Review verified identity/admin-claim requirements separately; the emulator proposal tests denial of an unverified email fallback.

findings.issue: A published Storage download token permits a read even when the SDK is denied by rules.
findings.recommendation: Do not publish private object tokens; inventory/revoke existing tokens when a production conversion is separately approved.

findings.check: The Update Bypass / Type Safety / Storage Abuse
findings.issue: Catalog create/update rules share the admin check but do not validate schemas or field sizes. Storage does bound upload size and content type. No ordinary-user write bypass was demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Validate public projection schemas at the trusted publisher, with matching defensive rules in the approved production design.
